status: partial — the Sermon on the Mount (chapters 5-7) only
note: Indexed on Matthew's own structure — the five discourses and the narrative blocks between them — beginning with the first discourse. Practice tags are assigned from the definitions in WMT A1, not from practice names.
synoptic_note: Entries carry an optional synoptic_parallel field recording the corresponding passage in Luke. This is a cross-reference, not a source claim. WMT G02 records the commitment to Q reconstruction as a stage the project passed through and no longer endorses, and WMT G09 cautions against reintroducing it as load-bearing without deliberately reversing that decision. Organizing this index around reconstructed Q pericopes would reintroduce it structurally, so pericope boundaries follow Matthew's own arrangement and the parallels are recorded alongside as data. The parallels were identified using Dr. Tabor's freely distributed Q arrangement, which presents its English text in the RSV; nothing from that document is quoted here, and all scripture is WEB, per the standing rule in WMT G10.

entries.pericope: The Beatitudes
entries.connection: The road's destination described as a set of conditions rather than achievements — poor in spirit, mourning, gentle, hungry, merciful, pure, peacemaking. Mercy is the only one whose reward is itself in kind, which is the reciprocity C03 builds its blueprint on.

entries.pericope: Salt and light; a city on a hill
entries.connection: Visibility is stated as a fact about the thing rather than as an ambition — a city on a hill cannot be hidden. The Citizen-Stranger given its outward face: full presence in the world, with the good works seen and the glory redirected.

entries.pericope: Not to destroy the law but to fulfill
entries.connection: Continuity with the older moral order asserted before any of it is intensified. The whole Sermon depends on this: what follows raises the standard rather than replacing it, which is the structural claim C01 makes about the moral order being a structure and not a menu.

entries.pericope: Anger, and leaving the gift at the altar
entries.connection: The prohibition is moved upstream from the act to the anger, and then reconciliation is ranked above worship — leave the gift, go, and come back. The Architecture of Peace given priority over liturgy itself, and the movement is required of the one who remembers, not the one who was wronged.

entries.pericope: The lustful gaze; the eye and the hand
entries.connection: The offense relocated to the interior movement that precedes it, which is the definition of nepsis rather than an intensification of the rule. The severity of the remedy measures how early the watchman is meant to be posted.

entries.pericope: Divorce
entries.connection: A concession in the older law is narrowed rather than expanded, and the consequence is stated in terms of what it does to the other person. Household fidelity treated as an obligation with a victim, not as a private arrangement.

entries.pericope: Do not swear at all; let your Yes be Yes
entries.connection: Oaths abolished on the grounds that reliable speech makes them unnecessary. The same instruction James 5:12 carries and the Didache sets against the double tongue — speech that needs no reinforcement because it is already true.

entries.pericope: Turn the other cheek; go the second mile
entries.connection: Retaliation is not merely forbidden but replaced by a surplus — the other cheek, the cloak as well, the second mile. Non-Retaliation and Absorbing the Blow given their governing text, and the Didache's opening chapter draws directly on it.

entries.pericope: Love your enemies; he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good
entries.connection: The circle of concern widened to its limit and then grounded in how sun and rain are distributed. Shedding Harshness given its summit text: loving those who love you is named as the ordinary human floor, not the standard.

entries.pericope: Let your merciful deeds be in secret
entries.connection: Almsgiving commanded and then stripped of its audience — the left hand kept ignorant of the right. Habitual Almsgiving and the Hidden Life joined in one instruction, which is why generosity here cannot double as reputation.

entries.pericope: The inner room, and the Lord's Prayer
entries.connection: The Secret Place given as a physical instruction — a room, a shut door — followed by the prayer the Didache directs be said three times daily. The Daily Anchors and the Secret Rhythmic Devotion both take their text from here, and the forgiveness clause is the only petition Jesus returns to afterward.

entries.pericope: When you fast, anoint your head
entries.connection: Discipline required to be concealed rather than displayed, with the concealment made active — wash, anoint, look ordinary. The Hidden Life stated as method: the practice is kept, and the appearance of keeping it is deliberately removed.

entries.pericope: Treasure, the sound eye, and two masters
entries.connection: Three images for a single claim: what you hold determines what you see and whom you serve. The heart is said to follow the treasure rather than direct it, which is why C07 treats cleansed sight as a matter of attachment before it is a matter of judgment.

entries.pericope: The birds, the lilies, and tomorrow's anxiety
entries.connection: Anxiety answered by observation rather than argument — look at the birds, consider the lilies. The Discipline of Unknowing applied to the future, and the closing instruction limits the day's burden to the day itself.

entries.pericope: The speck and the beam
entries.connection: Correction of another is made conditional on prior self-examination, and the disproportion is comic on purpose. The Moral Audit and Self-Accusation given their common text — the sequence is not optional, and sight of the other's fault is said to depend on it.

entries.pericope: Pearls before pigs
entries.connection: A restraint on giving what is true to those who will trample it, placed immediately after the prohibition on judging. The same triage Proverbs 9:7-8 applies to reproof — some true words are withheld, and withholding is not cowardice.

entries.pericope: Ask, seek, knock
entries.connection: Three verbs of increasing insistence, answered by an argument from ordinary fatherhood. Persistence in asking treated as normal rather than presumptuous, which is the posture the Daily Anchors assume.

entries.pericope: Whatever you desire that men do to you
entries.connection: The whole law compressed into one reversible test, stated positively rather than as a prohibition. The Didache opens with its negative form; this is the version that requires action rather than restraint.

entries.pericope: The narrow gate
entries.connection: The Two Ways in the form C01 takes its architecture from, and the same figure the Didache opens with. The narrow way is described as hard to find rather than hard to walk, which locates the difficulty in perception.

entries.pericope: By their fruits you will know them
entries.connection: The test C08 is built on, given as the only reliable instrument against a teacher whose appearance is deliberately reassuring. Sheep's clothing means the disguise is competent, so nothing but outcome will serve.

entries.pericope: Not everyone who says Lord, Lord
entries.connection: Prophecy, exorcism, and mighty works are all conceded and all found insufficient. The proof test of C12 pushed to its hardest form — impressive fruit is not the same as doing the will, and the passage refuses to soften that.

entries.pericope: The house on rock and the house on sand
entries.connection: Both men hear; only one does. The storm is identical for both, which removes circumstance as the variable and leaves only whether the words were acted on — the Moral Audit's premise, and the reason the Sermon ends here rather than on a promise.
